# Every configuration key

This page lists every key FerroEHR reads from `ferroehr.toml`, generated from the configuration
types, so it always matches the server you run. Each section is one TOML table. A key without a
default is unset until you set it. Every key can also be set as an environment variable: `FERROEHR`,
then the TOML path with `__` between the segments, such as `FERROEHR__DATABASE__MAX_CONNECTIONS`.

The shipped `ferroehr.toml` holds only the keys an operator usually sets. The guides under
[Configuration reference](configuration.md) explain the sections.

## `[deployment]`

The declared posture, the openEHR specification set and the licence token.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profile` | `"sandbox"` or `"production"` | `"sandbox"` | The declared posture (`sandbox` \| `production`; default `sandbox`). `production` refuses to start while a separation it asserts is missing and not accepted by name (#3226). |
| `accepts` | array of `"shared_credential"` or `"shared_cluster"` or `"open_subject_namespace"` or `"audit_off"` or `"audit_fails_open"` or `"no_category_map"` or `"open_ehr_access_default"` or `"migrate_on_runtime_credential"` or `"auth_off"` or `"rbac_off"` or `"plaintext_listener"` or `"plaintext_audit_feed"` or `"plaintext_object_store"` | `[]` | The `DeploymentGap`s a `production` deployment runs without, each stated on every boot and on `/management/status`. Ignored under `sandbox`, which accepts everything. |
| `spec_profile` | `"stable"` or `"development"` | `"development"` | The openEHR specification generation set the server runs (`development` \| `stable`; default `development`). |
| `licence_file` | string | unset | The commercial licence token file the licensor issued. Optional in every respect: an unset, missing, malformed or expired token is logged once at boot and the server runs unlicensed, identically in every other way. |

## `[server]`

The HTTP listener: the family's section (the listen address, the timeouts, the body limit, the
overload bound, the drain, TLS, the trusted proxies, the caller rate and compression).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `listen` | string | `"0.0.0.0:8080"` | The socket address the listener binds. |
| `base_path` | string | `""` | The path every route is served under: empty, or starting with `/` and not ending with one. |
| `request_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long one request may take before the server answers `408`. |
| `header_read_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a client may take to send its first byte once it connected, and each HTTP/1.1 request head from that head's first byte; a client still sending its head then is disconnected, which bounds a connection that never finishes one. Never zero. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"2min"` | How long a kept-alive HTTP/1.1 connection may wait for its next request before the server closes it. Keep it longer than the idle timeout of the clients and proxies in front, so they close an idle connection first. Never zero. |
| `body_limit` | size | `"64MiB"` | The largest request body the server reads before answering `413`. |
| `drain_delay` | duration | `"0s"` | How long readiness stays withdrawn before the listener closes, so an orchestrator stops sending requests first. |
| `shutdown_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long the requests in flight may take once the listener closed. |
| `max_concurrent_requests` | integer | unset | How many requests the server serves at once; past it a request is answered `503`. Unset, there is no bound. |
| `retry_after` | duration | `"1s"` | How long a refused request is told to wait (`Retry-After`), a whole number of seconds, since the header carries delay-seconds (RFC 9110 §10.2.3). |
| `trusted_proxies` | array of string | `[]` | The reverse proxies whose forwarded client address is believed, each an address or a CIDR block; empty, every request is named by its peer. |
| `forwarded_header` | `"forwarded"` or `"x-forwarded-for"` | `"forwarded"` | The header a trusted proxy names the client in. |
| `compression` | boolean | `true` | Whether a response is compressed with gzip or Brotli when the client accepts one. |
| `compression_min_size` | size | `"1KiB"` | The smallest response body that is compressed. |

## `[server.tls]`

The listener's TLS; unset, the listener speaks plain HTTP behind a proxy that terminates TLS.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `certificate_file` | string | required | The certificate chain, the leaf first. |
| `key_file` | string | required | The private key of the leaf. |
| `client_auth` | `"none"` or `"optional"` or `"required"` | `"none"` | Whether the listener asks a client certificate. |
| `client_ca_file` | string | unset | The CA bundle a client certificate must chain to; required unless `client_auth` is `none`, and refused when it is. |
| `reload_interval` | string | unset | How often the files are read again, never zero; unset, only `SIGHUP` reads them again. |
| `healthcheck_identity_file` | string | unset | The client certificate chain and key, in one PEM, the healthcheck presents to a listener that asks one. |
| `min_version` | `"1.2"` or `"1.3"` | `"1.3"` | The oldest TLS version the listener speaks: `"1.3"` unless lowered to `"1.2"`. |

## `[server.caller_rate]`

The requests one caller may send; unset, a caller is not limited.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requests_per_second` | integer | required | The requests per second a caller may send once its burst is spent. |
| `burst` | integer | required | The requests a caller may send at once. |

The console, the request log and the OpenTelemetry export, the family's shared section.

|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | `"auto"` or `"json"` or `"pretty"` | `"auto"` | The console rendering. |
| `filter` | string | `"info,hyper=warn,tower=warn,h2=warn"` | The `tracing` filter directive of the console. |

| `environment` | string | unset | The deployment environment, `deployment.environment.name` on the resource, such as `production`. |

## `[telemetry.otlp]`

The OTLP collector, when spans and metrics are exported.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string | `""` | The collector's OTLP/gRPC endpoint; `https://` speaks TLS. It may carry a credential, so it renders masked. |
| `traces` | boolean | `true` | Whether the product's spans are exported. |
| `metrics` | boolean | `true` | Whether the metrics are pushed. |
| `sample_ratio` | number | `1.0` | The share of the server's traces that are sampled. |

## `[telemetry.otlp.tls]`

The TLS to the collector: trust roots beside the platform's, the client identity for mutual TLS and
the minimum version. The crate reads none of it: the product reads the table with
`ferrohealth-server`'s `TlsClient` and hands the built configuration to `Telemetry::with_tls`. TLS
material is refused beside an endpoint that is not `https://`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client_identity` | string | unset | The client certificate chain and its private key, in one PEM. |
| `client_identity_file` | string | unset | A file holding `client_identity`. |
| `trust_roots_file` | string | unset | A PEM bundle of trust roots beside the platform's. |
| `min_version` | `"1.2"` or `"1.3"` | `"1.3"` | The oldest TLS version the client speaks: `"1.3"` unless lowered to `"1.2"`, as for the listener. |

## `[auth]`

Authentication: the `ferrohealth-smart` section, whose serialization writes every secret as `***`,
`[auth.idp]`, `[auth.smart]` and `[auth.scim]`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Whether inbound authentication is on; a product may refuse `false`. |
| `realm` | string | `""` | The realm the challenges name; empty for none, which a product replaces with its own default. |
| `capabilities` | array of string | `[]` | The SMART capabilities the discovery document adds, each a capability SMART App Launch 2.2.0 or the SMART on openEHR draft defines, or a full URI. |
| `scopes_supported` | array of string | `[]` | The scopes the discovery document lists as `scopes_supported`: only scopes the product honours, because "the server SHALL support all scopes listed here". |
| `product_scope` | string | `""` | The product's own scope, a full URI or a string starting with `__`; empty for none. |

## `[auth.smart]`

The SMART App Launch resource-server posture.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `discovery` | boolean | `false` | Serve the `/.well-known/smart-configuration` discovery document (SMART App Launch 2.x §Conformance; default `false`). The document is built from one `[auth]` issuer's metadata: the issuer `Self::issuer_metadata_file` names, else the first whose metadata is read from it, else the first. |
| `issuer_metadata_file` | string | unset | The RFC 8414 §2 authorization-server metadata of the `[auth]` issuer it names, whose key set is a `jwks_file` and carries none: a JSON document read at boot. SMART App Launch 2.2.0, Conformance, §Metadata requires the `token_endpoint` it names. |
| `platform_base_url` | string | unset | The SMART platform base URL the discovery document hangs off (master04 §Service Discovery: the document is served relative to the platform or gateway base, not the FHIR base). Unset, the REST root (`/ferroehr/rest`). A leading path segment is honoured, e.g. `/gateway/v1` → `/gateway/v1/.well-known/smart-configuration`. |
| `public_base_url` | string | unset | The server's externally reachable origin (scheme + host [+ port]), e.g. `https://cdr.example.com`. master04 §Services makes every `services.*` entry's `baseUrl` an "Absolute URL to the root of the API (required)", so the document prefixes this origin onto the served base paths. Required when `Self::discovery` is set. |
| `episode_launch` | boolean | `false` | Episode context (master09 §Experimental: Episode Context), advertised only: `episode_launch = true` adds `context-openehr-episode` to the document's capabilities and applies no episode filtering (openEHR has no first-class Episode resource; master09 calls the semantics "currently implementation-defined"). |
| `backend_clients` | array of string | `[]` | The `client_id`s of the backend clients a `system/aql-*` grant counts for: master08 §Resource Scopes says such a grant "would grant access to all registered and ad-hoc AQL queries system-wide". Empty, no client. |
| `patient_issuers` | array of string | `[]` | The issuers whose `patient/` grants count, each confined to the `ehrId` of the token's launch context (master07 §Context Selection: the `ehrId` names an EHR of the platform that issued it). Empty, a `patient/` grant grants nothing. |
| `demographic_clients` | array of string | `[]` | The `client_id`s that reach the DEMOGRAPHIC API. master08 §Resource Scopes defines no resource family for demographic data, so no SMART scope covers it: a listed client, or a caller holding the `[auth] product_scope`, reaches it (no openEHR spec governs this: our own design). |

## `[auth.scim]`

The SCIM 2.0 service provider and its provisioning clients; absent, `/scim/v2/` is not served.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `public_base_url` | string | unset | The externally reachable origin the SCIM base URL hangs off, such as `https://cdr.example.com`; every `meta.location` and discovery document names `<public_base_url>/scim/v2` (RFC 7643 §3.1: `location` is "The URI of the resource being returned"). Required. |
| `filter_max_results` | integer | `100` | The most resources one list response returns (RFC 7643 §5, the `ServiceProviderConfig` `filter.maxResults`). |
| `max_deactivations` | integer | `100` | The most Users one client deactivates or deletes in one window; past it, a deactivation or a deletion is refused with `429`. |
| `deactivation_window` | duration | `"1h"` | The length of that window. |
| `contact_erasure_delay` | duration | `"0s"` | How long after a User's deletion the contacts of every version of its `PERSON` are erased (GDPR Art. 17), at most 30 days; `"0s"` erases them in the deletion itself. The name, the binding key and the identifiers stay. |
| `max_group_members` | integer | `5000` | The most members one Group holds; an add past it is refused with `400`. Each membership change stores every membership of the Group again (RM demographic master02 §Versioning Semantics), so the cap bounds a Group's version storage. |

RBAC, ABAC, assurance, the party binding, the system clients, the federation agreements and the
registered origins.

The table holds only the tables below.

## `[authz.rbac]`

Role-based access control.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Master switch of the coarse role gate, active only when auth is enabled (`FERROEHR__AUTHZ__RBAC__ENABLED`, default `true`). |
| `admin_role` | string | `"ADMIN"` | The role required for Admin-class operations (default `ADMIN`). |
| `readonly_role` | string | `"READONLY"` | The role marking a principal as read-only (default `READONLY`): a caller carrying it is refused on every write operation even when it also holds granting roles (a restriction overrides a grant). Supports the conformance catalogue's authorization-separation cases. |
| `subject_audit_role` | string | unset | The role that may read the access log for ONE subject at a time (`FERROEHR__AUTHZ__RBAC__SUBJECT_AUDIT_ROLE`, default unset). |
| `emergency_access_role` | string | unset | The role that may reach data under an EHDS Art. 8 access restriction in an emergency (`FERROEHR__AUTHZ__RBAC__EMERGENCY_ACCESS_ROLE`, default unset). |
| `access_service_roles` | array of string | `[]` | The roles of an EHDS Art. 10 access-service caller, held to an opt-out (`FERROEHR__AUTHZ__RBAC__ACCESS_SERVICE_ROLES`; empty, the default, holds nobody). |
| `identifier_reader_role` | string | unset | The role that may read a party's protected national identifiers (`FERROEHR__AUTHZ__RBAC__IDENTIFIER_READER_ROLE`, default unset). |
| `import_role` | string | unset | The role that may import an EHR or an EHR extract (`message_import_ehr`, `message_import_ehr_extract`; default unset). |
| `role_issuers` | array of string | `[]` | The issuers whose role claims may grant `admin_role`, `emergency_access_role`, `import_role` and `identifier_reader_role`, each a `persons` issuer; empty, the default, lets no token grant them. |
| `ehr_access_default` | `"open"` or `"restricted"` | `"open"` | What an EHR carrying no `ACCESS_CONTROL_SETTINGS` admits (default `open`). |

Attribute-based access control (opt-in).

|---|---|---|---|

| `engine` | `"cedar"` or `"remote"` | `"cedar"` | Which PDP engine to use (default `cedar`). |

## `[authz.abac.remote]`

Remote-PDP settings.

The table holds only the tables below.

## `[authz.abac.remote.endpoint]`

`[authz.abac.remote.endpoint]`, the family's outbound endpoint: the PDP base URL (`url`; the policy
name is appended, so it must end with `/`; required when `engine = remote`), the timeouts (a connect
timeout keeps a PDP that blackholes packets from parking the request until the OS TCP timeout), the
`retry` of a call that got no answer or a `5xx`, the TLS and the credential, such as the OAuth 2.0
client credentials grant. Any `userinfo` in the URL is masked in every rendering.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | `""` | The service's URL (RFC 3986); required. It renders with its userinfo and its query masked, in `Debug` and when serialized. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"5s"` | How long one whole call may take; never zero. |
| `connect_timeout` | string | `"2s"` | How long opening the connection may take; unset, only `timeout` bounds it. |

## `[authz.abac.remote.endpoint.retry]`

How a failed call is tried again.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_attempts` | integer | `3` | How many times one call is tried in all; 1 tries once. |
| `initial_backoff` | duration | `"200ms"` | The wait before the second try. |
| `max_backoff` | duration | `"5s"` | The longest wait between two tries. |

## `[authz.abac.remote.endpoint.credentials.onward]`

The onward target the lane reaches on a caller's behalf, authenticating with `oauth`.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string | `""` | The identifier of the issuer of the onward tokens, whose metadata names its token endpoint unless `token_endpoint` is set. |
| `kind` | `"persons"` or `"patients"` or `"machines"` or `"federation"` | unset | Whose tokens the issuer signs: `persons` (a delegated exchange), `patients` (a patient's own token) or `federation`; required, with no default. |
| `profile` | `"rfc9068"` or `"entra"` or `"keycloak"` or `"okta"` or `"nl"` | `"rfc9068"` | The preset the issuer's profile starts from. |
| `token_endpoint` | string | `""` | The token endpoint itself; empty to discover it from `issuer`. It renders with its userinfo and its query masked. |
| `client_id` | string | `""` | The client id at this issuer; empty for the lane's own. |
| `audiences` | array of string | `[]` | The audiences an onward token may name, at least one. |
| `indicators` | array of string | `[]` | The `resource` or `audience` values the request names, as the profile's `onward_indicator` says. |
| `scope` | string | `""` | The `scope` the request names; empty for none. |
| `correlation_claim` | string | `""` | The claim a chained federation route carries from the subject token to the onward token; empty for none. |
| `cache` | boolean | `true` | Whether the lane holds the tokens it obtains until they near their `exp`. `false` exchanges a token at the issuer on every call, a setting for a performance measurement's self-test, never for production. `true` by default. |
| `actor_assertion` | boolean | `false` | Whether every token exchange sent without an actor token names the lane's client as its actor with an assertion signed by the current key of its `oauth` table's key ring (RFC 8693 §2.1; `Onward::with_actor_assertion`). `false` by default. |

## `[[authz.federation.agreement]]`

The agreements, one per issuer and accessor.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string | `""` | The `federation` issuer of the external callers. |
| `accessor` | `"person"` or `"organisation"` | unset | Who the agreement admits: named persons, or the organisation. |
| `name` | string | `""` | The agreement's name. |
| `version` | string | `""` | The agreement's version. |
| `jurisdiction` | string | `""` | The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 jurisdiction; a `profile = "nl"` issuer implies `NL`. |
| `exchange` | string | `""` | The kind of exchange the agreement covers. |
| `purpose` | `"care"` or `"keuring"` | unset | What the exchange is for; required of an NL agreement, which may not serve a keuring (Wabvpz Art. 15f(2)). |
| `consent` | `"mitz"` or `"local"` | unset | The source of the consent the exchange is conditioned on, never its legal ground. |
| `reads` | array of string | `[]` | The most an external caller may read: `patient/` scopes only. |
| `writes` | array of string | `[]` | The template ids an external person may commit; none by default. |
| `discard` | boolean | `false` | Whether an external person may discard a dispensation of the same point of care within `discard_window`. |
| `discard_window` | duration | `"1d"` | The window of a discard, a whole number of hours (MyHealth@EU Requirements Catalogue 10.0.0, requirement 07.04, sets `"24h"`). |
| `ehdsi_service` | `"patient_summary"` or `"eprescription"` or `"orcd"` | unset | The MyHealth@EU service a contact point's person agreement serves, which names the `*_NOT_FOUND` code of a request outside the TRC patient; required on a `contact_point` issuer and refused elsewhere. |
| `opt_out_override` | boolean | `false` | Whether a professional of the agreement may read an opted-out EHR where national law provides the EHDS Art. 10(2) vital-interest access. |
| `access_class` | `"automated"` or `"chained"` | unset | For an organisation: whether no natural person views the data, or the requester logs the person. |
| `chained_log_retention` | string | unset | For a `chained` access: how long the requester keeps its log, a calendar period (`"P5Y"`). |

The origins of data this deployment recognises, which a retention period and an access rule may name

| `clients` | array of string | `[]` | The authenticated clients whose direct commits come from this origin: a Basic user name, or the `client_id` (failing that the `azp`) of an OAuth 2.0 access token (RFC 9068 §2.2). Each client belongs to one origin at most. |

## `[api]`

The openEHR REST API: the base path, the system identifier, the `OPTIONS` identity, the `OpenAPI`
UI, CORS, the clinical body tier and the ADMIN and terminology groups.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_path` | string | `"/ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1"` | The ITS-REST base path all API routes hang off, from the root of the listener. `management.base_path` is set the same way; the two never overlap. |
| `openapi_ui` | `"off"` or `"admin_only"` or `"private"` or `"public"` | `"private"` | Who may read the Swagger UI and the `OpenAPI` documents at the REST root: `off` (not mounted), `admin_only`, `private` (any authenticated principal; the default) or `public`. The documents list the whole enabled operation surface, admin and message groups included, so `public` discloses it to anyone who can reach the port. The same vocabulary the management endpoints use; the name is the `OpenAPI` Specification's, the document the UI renders. |
| `system_id` | string | `"ferroehr.local"` | This CDR's own openEHR **system identifier** — the identity the deployment stamps into the data it authors (`FERROEHR__API__SYSTEM_ID`). |
| `body_limit` | string | unset | The largest body the ordinary clinical surface accepts, below the listener's `server.body_limit`. |
| `admin` | boolean | `false` | Whether the ADMIN API group is served. |
| `terminology` | boolean | `false` | Whether the terminology extension API is mounted. Off by default — the routes answer `404` unless enabled. The terminology server the CDR asks is `[terminology]`. |

## `[api.cors]`

The CORS protocol answers of the API (Fetch Standard §3.2). Absent, no CORS header is sent, so a
browser on another origin cannot read a response.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_origins` | array of string | `[]` | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`: the origins a browser may read responses for, each a serialized origin such as `https://app.example`, or `["*"]` for any origin (dev only). |
| `allow_methods` | array of string | `[]` | `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`: the methods a preflight admits; empty admits the method the preflight asks for. |
| `allow_headers` | array of string | `[]` | `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`: the request headers a preflight admits; empty admits the headers the preflight asks for. |
| `expose_headers` | array of string | `[]` | `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`: the response headers a script may read beyond the CORS-safelisted ones. |
| `allow_credentials` | boolean | `false` | `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`: whether a credentialed request's response may be read. Refused beside `allow_origins = ["*"]`, which the Fetch Standard forbids together. |
| `max_age` | string | unset | `Access-Control-Max-Age`: how long a preflight answer may be cached; unset sends no header. |

## `[api.options]`

The `OPTIONS /` System-Options manifest identity (`[api.options]`). Sourced from config so the
public identity is not a string literal in the handler; the live endpoint list is supplied
separately by `ferroehr_rest::router`. This is the *display* identity of the manifest — the
data-authoring identity is `Self::system_id`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `solution` | string | `"FerroEHR"` | `Options.solution` — the product name. |
| `vendor` | string | `"Cadasto B.V."` | `Options.vendor` — the organisation providing the solution (ITS-REST `specifications/schemas/others/Options.yaml`, a plain string); defaults to the manufacturer's name (`crate::manufacturer::MANUFACTURER`). |

## `[database]`

The shared `PostgreSQL` DSN, pool tuning, migrations and one table per storage domain.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | secret URL | `"postgres://***@localhost:5432/ferroehr"` | `PostgreSQL` connection DSN (`postgres://user:pass@host:port/db`). Credentials are redacted from every rendering (`SecretUrl`). |
| `url_file` | string | unset | Path to a file holding the DSN, read at boot in place of `Self::url`. |
| `migrate_url` | string | unset | DSN that schema preparation (`prepare`) authenticates as; unset (the default) reuses `Self::url`. |
| `migrate_url_file` | string | unset | Path to a file holding `Self::migrate_url`, read at boot in place of it — the mounted-secret route, as `Self::url_file` is for the clinical DSN. Setting both is a boot error. |
| `max_connections` | integer | `20` | Upper bound of the connection pool. |
| `min_connections` | integer | `2` | Connections the pool keeps open when idle (avoids cold reopen + `SET search_path` churn under variable load). |
| `acquire_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long to wait for a free connection before failing. |
| `statement_timeout` | duration | `"1min"` | `statement_timeout` applied to every pooled connection; `"0s"` leaves the server default (usually unlimited). |
| `migrations` | `"apply"` or `"verify"` | `"apply"` | Whether the server applies its embedded migrations at boot (`MigrationMode`). |

## `[management]`

The management/observability surface.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Master switch. When `false`, no management routes are mounted at all. |
| `base_path` | string | `"/management"` | The base path the management endpoints hang off. |
| `listen` | string | unset | When set, the management surface is served from its **own** listener on this socket address (a separate axum server task in the binary) instead of the main API listener — so production can keep it off the public listener entirely. The same form as `server.listen`. |
| `flame_file` | string | unset | Span-timing capture: every span's folded stacks are written to this file, for `inferno-flamegraph` to render offline. Unset, nothing is captured. |

Per-endpoint access levels — the SINGLE authority for this surface.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `metrics` | `"off"` or `"admin_only"` or `"private"` or `"public"` | `"off"` | `/management/metrics` (+ `/{name}`) — the JSON registry view. |
| `prometheus` | `"off"` or `"admin_only"` or `"private"` or `"public"` | `"off"` | `/management/prometheus` — the text exposition scraped by Prometheus. |
| `env` | `"off"` or `"admin_only"` or `"private"` or `"public"` | `"off"` | `/management/env` — the redacted effective configuration. |
| `loggers` | `"off"` or `"admin_only"` or `"private"` or `"public"` | `"off"` | `/management/loggers` — the runtime `EnvFilter` control. |
| `flamegraph` | `"off"` or `"admin_only"` or `"private"` or `"public"` | `"off"` | `/management/flamegraph` — the on-demand CPU flamegraph (pprof sampling). |
| `health` | `"off"` or `"admin_only"` or `"private"` or `"public"` | `"off"` | `/management/health` — every readiness indicator with its detail. |
| `status` | `"off"` or `"admin_only"` or `"private"` or `"public"` | `"off"` | `/management/status` — the status document with the licence, the deployment posture and the support period. |

## `[audit]`

The IHE ATNA audit trail / System Log (local Audit Record Repository + the syslog and FHIR-feed
forwarding sinks).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Master switch (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__ENABLED`). **On by default** — every deployment gets a queryable audit trail with zero external dependencies (the sinks decide where records go). |
| `enterprise_site_id` | string | unset | Enterprise/site id → `AuditEnterpriseSiteID` (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__ENTERPRISE_SITE_ID`). |
| `source_id` | string | `"ferroehr"` | Audit source id → `AuditSourceID` and the destination participant (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SOURCE_ID`). |
| `value_if_missing` | string | `"UNKNOWN"` | Fill value for empty mandatory fields (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__VALUE_IF_MISSING`). |
| `suppress_login_events` | boolean | `true` | Skip successful-login records (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SUPPRESS_LOGIN_EVENTS`). Rejected accesses (401/403) are always recorded. |
| `fail_mode` | `"open"` or `"closed"` | `"open"` | Failure mode (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__FAIL_MODE`): `open` \| `closed`. |
| `resolve_subject` | boolean | `true` | Enrich the patient participant via a background indexed lookup of `ehr.subject_id` (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__RESOLVE_SUBJECT`). On by default — the IHE BALP `Patient*` patterns and the patient-centric audit search need the subject; the lookup runs only on the background drain. |
| `queue_capacity` | integer | `8192` | Bounded audit queue capacity (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__QUEUE_CAPACITY`). Sized for write-path bursts: the drain persists in multi-row batches, so the queue only needs to ride out sink latency spikes, but a loaded write path can enqueue thousands per second. |
| `server_host` | string | unset | This node's advertised network address → the destination network-access-point (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SERVER_HOST`); the `value_if_missing` fill when unset. |
| `purpose_header` | string | `"x-purpose-of-use"` | The request header carrying the caller's declared purpose of use (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__PURPOSE_HEADER`), recorded on every access record. |
| `permit_header` | string | `"x-data-permit"` | The request header carrying the data permit the caller acts under (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__PERMIT_HEADER`), recorded on every access record. |
| `purpose_codes` | array of string | `[]` | The purpose codes this deployment accepts (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__PURPOSE_CODES`). |
| `emergency_purpose_codes` | array of string | `[]` | The declared purpose codes that mark an access as an emergency access (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__EMERGENCY_PURPOSE_CODES`). Empty (the default) marks nothing. |
| `legal_basis` | string | unset | The legal basis this deployment processes under (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__LEGAL_BASIS`), recorded on every access record. |

## `[audit.categories]`

The template and archetype map every access is classified through by EHDS priority category (Annex
II 3.2(c)). Empty by default, so the map FerroEHR ships applies; an unmapped access is recorded
`unclassified`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shipped_map` | boolean | `true` | Whether the map FerroEHR ships applies while this section declares no template and no archetype (`shipped_map`, on by default). Off with nothing declared, no map applies and every access is recorded `unclassified`, which `deployment.profile = "production"` refuses as the `no_category_map` gap. |
| `national` | array of string | `[]` | The national categories (Art. 14(1) third subparagraph), each `<system>\|<code>`. |
| `templates` | table of `"none"` or array of string | `{}` | Template id → categories (`[audit.categories.templates]`), consulted first. |
| `archetypes` | table of `"none"` or array of string | `{}` | Archetype id → categories (`[audit.categories.archetypes]`), consulted for an object whose template the map does not name. |

## `[audit.store]`

The local Audit Record Repository.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Persist every record locally (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__ENABLED`). **On by default** (owner posture: compliance out of the box). |
| `retention` | string | unset | How long records are kept, a calendar period (`"P5Y"`, `"P1830D"`); unset keeps them forever (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__RETENTION`). Applied hourly by the retention reaper. |
| `sgb_v_309_controller` | boolean | `false` | Whether this deployment is one of the controllers SGB V § 307 names for a German telematics-infrastructure application (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__SGB_V_309_CONTROLLER`). **Off by default.** |
| `verify_interval` | duration | `"1h"` | The time between two scheduled verifications of the store's hash chain (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__VERIFY_INTERVAL`); `"0s"` turns the schedule off. Default one hour. |
| `full_verify_interval` | duration | `"7d"` | The time between two scheduled full passes over the hash chain (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__FULL_VERIFY_INTERVAL`), which also recompute the records before the checkpoint; `"0s"` leaves the full pass to `SELECT * FROM audit.verify_audit_chain()` on demand. Default one week. A run that found damage is always followed by a full pass. |

## `[audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.credentials.oauth]`

The client credentials grant.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string | `""` | The issuer whose metadata names the token endpoint; exclusive with `token_endpoint`. |
| `token_endpoint` | string | `""` | The token endpoint itself; exclusive with `issuer`. It renders with its userinfo and its query masked. |
| `client_id` | string | `""` | The client identifier. |
| `client_auth` | `"client_secret_basic"` or `"client_secret_post"` or `"private_key_jwt"` or `"tls_client_auth"` or `"self_signed_tls_client_auth"` | `"client_secret_basic"` | How the client authenticates. |
| `client_secret` | string | unset | The client secret, rendered redacted. |
| `client_secret_file` | string | unset | The file holding the client secret. |
| `private_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file holding the private key of the client assertion under `private_key_jwt`, and of the actor assertion of an onward exchange (`credentials.onward.actor_assertion`) whatever the client authentication. |
| `kid` | string | `""` | The `kid` the assertion names; the RFC 7638 thumbprint when empty. |
| `assertion_alg` | string | unset | The algorithm the assertion is signed with; when unset, by key type, an EC key by its curve (P-256 ES256, P-384 ES384). |
| `scope` | string | `""` | The `scope` request parameter; empty for none. |
| `resource` | string | `""` | The RFC 8707 resource indicator; empty for none. |
| `audience` | string | `""` | The `audience` request parameter; empty for none. |
| `refresh_margin` | duration | `"30s"` | How long before the token expires a new one is fetched. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long one call to the authorization server may take. |
| `assertion_audience` | `"token_endpoint"` or `"issuer"` | `"token_endpoint"` | The `aud` of a `private_key_jwt` assertion: `token_endpoint` (the default) or `issuer`, which needs `issuer` set. |
| `dpop_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file of the `DPoP` key the tokens are bound to (RFC 9449). |
| `certificate_bound` | boolean | `false` | Whether the tokens are bound to the client certificate (RFC 8705 §3). |
| `security_profile` | `"oauth2"` or `"fapi2"` | `"oauth2"` | The security profile: `oauth2` (the default) or `fapi2`. |
| `mtls_alias_hosts` | array of string | `[]` | The hosts a FAPI 2.0 mutual-TLS alias may be on (RFC 8705 §5). |
| `previous_private_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file of the previous assertion key, published, never signing. |
| `previous_key_overlap` | duration | `"0s"` | How long the previous key stays published; `0s` for as long as it is set. |
| `next_private_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file of the next assertion key, published and never signing. |
| `authorization_details` | string | `""` | The RFC 9396 `authorization_details` JSON text; empty for none. |

The TLS of the token endpoint connection: trust roots beside the platform's, the client identity

## `[audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.credentials.onward]`

The onward target the lane reaches on a caller's behalf, authenticating with `oauth`.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string | `""` | The identifier of the issuer of the onward tokens, whose metadata names its token endpoint unless `token_endpoint` is set. |
| `kind` | `"persons"` or `"patients"` or `"machines"` or `"federation"` | unset | Whose tokens the issuer signs: `persons` (a delegated exchange), `patients` (a patient's own token) or `federation`; required, with no default. |
| `profile` | `"rfc9068"` or `"entra"` or `"keycloak"` or `"okta"` or `"nl"` | `"rfc9068"` | The preset the issuer's profile starts from. |
| `token_endpoint` | string | `""` | The token endpoint itself; empty to discover it from `issuer`. It renders with its userinfo and its query masked. |
| `client_id` | string | `""` | The client id at this issuer; empty for the lane's own. |
| `audiences` | array of string | `[]` | The audiences an onward token may name, at least one. |
| `indicators` | array of string | `[]` | The `resource` or `audience` values the request names, as the profile's `onward_indicator` says. |
| `scope` | string | `""` | The `scope` the request names; empty for none. |
| `correlation_claim` | string | `""` | The claim a chained federation route carries from the subject token to the onward token; empty for none. |
| `cache` | boolean | `true` | Whether the lane holds the tokens it obtains until they near their `exp`. `false` exchanges a token at the issuer on every call, a setting for a performance measurement's self-test, never for production. `true` by default. |
| `actor_assertion` | boolean | `false` | Whether every token exchange sent without an actor token names the lane's client as its actor with an assertion signed by the current key of its `oauth` table's key ring (RFC 8693 §2.1; `Onward::with_actor_assertion`). `false` by default. |

| `fields` | table of array of table | `{}` | The sources of each field, over the mapping's. |
| `countries` | array of string | `[]` | The country codes a professional may carry. |
| `issuing_authorities` | array of string | `[]` | The issuing authorities a professional or provider may name. |
| `provider_identifier_prefixes` | array of string | `[]` | The prefixes a healthcare provider identifier must start with. |
| `attests_authorization_details` | boolean | `false` | Whether the issuer attests the `authorization_details` it puts in a token, which RFC 9396 §12 has "sent through the user agent". |
| `authorization_details_type` | string | unset | The `authorization_details` type the attributes are read from. |
| `organisation_types` | array of string | `[]` | The `authorization_details` types that state an organisation's access. |
| `presentations_claim` | string | unset | The claim holding the Verifiable Presentations of a Nuts RFC021 §6 introspection response, `vps`. |
| `user_credential_types` | array of string | `[]` | The credential types the deployment declares user-authenticated. |
| `required_fields` | array of `"professional.family_name"` or `"professional.given_name"` or `"professional.name"` or `"professional.country_code"` or `"professional.hp_identifier"` or `"professional.issuing_authority_name"` or `"professional.hp_professional_role"` or `"professional.healthcare_provider_identifier"` or `"provider.healthcare_provider_identifier"` or `"provider.issuing_authority_name"` or `"provider.healthcare_provider_name"` or `"provider.healthcare_provider_address"` or `"purpose_of_use"` or `"assurance"` or `"nl.professional_number"` or `"nl.role"` or `"nl.ura"` or `"nl.organisation_type"` or `"professional.on_behalf_of"` or `"professional.authentication_method"` or `"professional.speciality"` or `"professional.npi"` or `"professional.permissions"` or `"provider.facility_type"` or `"provider.home_community_id"` or `"point_of_care"` or `"assertion.issuer"` or `"assertion.id"` or `"assertion.not_before"` or `"assertion.not_on_or_after"` or `"trc.id"` or `"trc.not_before"` or `"trc.not_on_or_after"` or `"patient.id"` or `"patient.id_source"` or `"patient.pid_issuer_country"` or `"consent.reference"` or `"correlation_id"` or `"assertion.name_id_format"` or `"message_id"` | `[]` | The fields every token of the issuer must carry, each with a source. |
| `requires_sender_constraint` | boolean | `false` | Whether the issuer's tokens must be sender-constrained, so the issuer fails to load without `sender_constraint = "required"`. |
| `exchanges_from` | array of string | `[]` | The subject-token issuers whose persons this issuer is trusted to map to its own, when it issues onward tokens (`client::onward`). |
| `person_mapping` | string | unset | The subject-token claim, a dotted path, whose value an onward token of this issuer must carry as `professional.hp_identifier`. |

An unknown key is a boot error naming it. |

The cross-domain cohort-query allow-list and limits.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `small_cell_threshold` | integer | `5` | The distinct-EHR floor a result set must reach to be served (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__COHORT__SMALL_CELL_THRESHOLD`); `0` disables suppression. |
| `max_cohort_size` | integer | `100000` | The largest cohort a predicate may select (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__COHORT__MAX_COHORT_SIZE`). |

The one cohort form an IHE patient identity source serves, so it turns the surface on without a bound predicate. |

The bound predicates, keyed by the name a caller uses (`[privacy.cohort.predicates]`). Empty — the
default — leaves the predicate half of the surface off.

|---|---|---|---|

| `node` | string | required | The ELEMENT's `archetype_node_id` at-code (`at0012`). |

## `[privacy.access_delay]`

The EHDS Art. 3(3) delay of the person's own access; absent, off.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `categories` | array of string | `[]` | The categories whose new compositions are held at creation, named as `[audit.categories]` names one: a priority category of Art. 14(1) by its code (`Laboratory-Reports`, `Medical-Imaging`, …) or as `<system>\|<code>`, or a national category the map declares (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__ACCESS_DELAY__CATEGORIES`, comma-separated). Empty holds nothing at creation, and a professional still holds an object by hand. |
| `max_delay` | string | unset | How long a hold lasts at most, a whole number of hours from `"1h"` to `MAX_HOURS` hours (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__ACCESS_DELAY__MAX_DELAY`): the length of a hold placed at creation and the latest end a professional may give one. Required. |

## `[record]`

The record itself: the subject index, versioning, signing, the query engine, the change feed and
multimedia.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subject_index` | `"pixm"` or `"local"` | unset | Who holds the subject-to-EHR cross-reference, the IHE patient identity source of `[pixm]` (`pixm`) or the in-instance map (`local`). No default: an unset index refuses the start. |

## `[record.versioning]`

The answer to an identical re-send.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `idempotent_resend` | boolean | `false` | `idempotent_resend` (default `false`): when `true`, an update whose content equals the current version's commits nothing and answers with the existing version's `ETag` and `Location`, leaving one `resend` record on the access log. No `commit_audit` and no CONTRIBUTION then record the act (RM common master06 §Committal and Audits), which is why the default records every commit. The name is RFC 9110 §9.2.2's: a re-send then has the effect of one request. |

## `[record.signing]`

VERSION signing.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Server-side signing of committed versions. Defaults **on** so the STANDARD "Signing" capability is demonstrably met. |
| `mode` | `"digest"` or `"pgp"` | `"digest"` | Signing mode: `digest` \| `pgp`. |
| `key_file` | string | unset | Armored RFC 4880 secret key; **required for `pgp` mode** (validated at boot, fail-closed). |
| `key_passphrase` | string | unset | Key passphrase, kept in `ferrohealth_secret::secret::Secret` and redacted from any config snapshot. |
| `key_passphrase_file` | string | unset | File-based indirection for `Self::key_passphrase` (K8s/Docker secrets). Exactly one of the pair may be set; the loader reads and trims the file. |
| `retired_key_files` | array of string | `[]` | Armored RFC 4880 **public** keys retired from signing but retained for verification, so versions signed before a key rotation keep verifying. |
| `verify_on_read` | `"off"` or `"warn"` or `"strict"` | unset | Read-time verification policy: `off` \| `warn` \| `strict`. **Unset** (the default) resolves via `Self::effective_verify_on_read` to `strict` when signing is enabled — the explicit "sign but never check" state is reachable only by deliberately setting `off`. |

## `[record.query]`

AQL execution knobs.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plan_cache_capacity` | integer | `256` | Max distinct cached query plans; `0` disables the plan cache (every lookup misses and the full parse→lower path runs). |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | Per-query DB execution budget; `"0s"` disables it. Overrun reports `408` (ITS-REST `Requests_and_responses` §HTTP status codes). |
| `max_result_rows` | integer | `10000` | The largest page of rows one query execution serves; `0` means unbounded. |

## `[record.change_feed]`

The commit-event outbox readers and their retention.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `readers` | array of string | `[]` | The readers of the outbox feed, each a name matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` (`ferrobridge`, for one). Boot registers each one and marks every reader the list no longer names inactive. Empty by default: no commit writes an outbox row. |
| `retention` | duration | `"7d"` | How long a row is kept once every active reader has acknowledged it, counted from its commit instant. |
| `prune_interval` | duration | `"1h"` | How often the retention prune runs. |

## `[record.multimedia]`

`DV_MULTIMEDIA` externalization to object storage. It keeps `enabled`, because its store applies
while it is off: blobs already offloaded are read back from `url`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Master switch. `false` (default) = today's inline behaviour, byte for byte; no object store is built or contacted. |
| `threshold` | size | `"256KiB"` | A decoded `DV_MULTIMEDIA.data` strictly larger than this is offloaded to the object store; at or below it stays inline. Default `"256KiB"`. |
| `url` | string | unset | S3-compatible endpoint URL (e.g. a SeaweedFS S3 gateway in dev/test, or an AWS/MinIO endpoint in prod). `None` uses the object_store default AWS endpoint resolution. Any `userinfo` in it is masked in every rendering. An `http://` URL is plain HTTP, which a dev SeaweedFS speaks; a `production` deployment names it as a gap. |
| `bucket` | string | `"openehr-multimedia"` | Target bucket for content-addressed blobs. |
| `region` | string | `"us-east-1"` | AWS region (S3 requires one even for non-AWS endpoints). |
| `access_key_id` | string | unset | Access key id. `None` (with `secret_access_key` also `None`) runs the client unsigned/anonymous — the mode a keyless dev SeaweedFS accepts. |
| `secret_access_key` | string | unset | Secret access key (paired with `access_key_id`); never rendered. |
| `secret_access_key_file` | string | unset | File-based indirection for `Self::secret_access_key` (K8s/Docker secrets). Exactly one of the pair may be set; the loader reads and trims the file. |

| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long one whole call may take; never zero. |
| `connect_timeout` | string | unset | How long opening the connection may take; unset, only `timeout` bounds it. |

| `max_backoff` | duration | `"5s"` | The longest wait between two tries. |

## `[terminology.endpoint.credentials.oauth]`

The client credentials grant.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string | `""` | The issuer whose metadata names the token endpoint; exclusive with `token_endpoint`. |
| `token_endpoint` | string | `""` | The token endpoint itself; exclusive with `issuer`. It renders with its userinfo and its query masked. |
| `client_id` | string | `""` | The client identifier. |
| `client_auth` | `"client_secret_basic"` or `"client_secret_post"` or `"private_key_jwt"` or `"tls_client_auth"` or `"self_signed_tls_client_auth"` | `"client_secret_basic"` | How the client authenticates. |
| `client_secret` | string | unset | The client secret, rendered redacted. |
| `client_secret_file` | string | unset | The file holding the client secret. |
| `private_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file holding the private key of the client assertion under `private_key_jwt`, and of the actor assertion of an onward exchange (`credentials.onward.actor_assertion`) whatever the client authentication. |
| `kid` | string | `""` | The `kid` the assertion names; the RFC 7638 thumbprint when empty. |
| `assertion_alg` | string | unset | The algorithm the assertion is signed with; when unset, by key type, an EC key by its curve (P-256 ES256, P-384 ES384). |
| `scope` | string | `""` | The `scope` request parameter; empty for none. |
| `resource` | string | `""` | The RFC 8707 resource indicator; empty for none. |
| `audience` | string | `""` | The `audience` request parameter; empty for none. |
| `refresh_margin` | duration | `"30s"` | How long before the token expires a new one is fetched. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long one call to the authorization server may take. |
| `assertion_audience` | `"token_endpoint"` or `"issuer"` | `"token_endpoint"` | The `aud` of a `private_key_jwt` assertion: `token_endpoint` (the default) or `issuer`, which needs `issuer` set. |
| `dpop_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file of the `DPoP` key the tokens are bound to (RFC 9449). |
| `certificate_bound` | boolean | `false` | Whether the tokens are bound to the client certificate (RFC 8705 §3). |
| `security_profile` | `"oauth2"` or `"fapi2"` | `"oauth2"` | The security profile: `oauth2` (the default) or `fapi2`. |
| `mtls_alias_hosts` | array of string | `[]` | The hosts a FAPI 2.0 mutual-TLS alias may be on (RFC 8705 §5). |
| `previous_private_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file of the previous assertion key, published, never signing. |
| `previous_key_overlap` | duration | `"0s"` | How long the previous key stays published; `0s` for as long as it is set. |
| `next_private_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file of the next assertion key, published and never signing. |
| `authorization_details` | string | `""` | The RFC 9396 `authorization_details` JSON text; empty for none. |

## `[terminology.endpoint.credentials.oauth.tls]`

The TLS of the token endpoint connection: trust roots beside the platform's, the client identity
presented over mutual TLS (RFC 8705 §2) and the minimum version. The crate reads none of it: a table
that names material resolves through the product's `TlsBuilder`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client_identity` | string | unset | The client certificate chain and its private key, in one PEM. |
| `client_identity_file` | string | unset | A file holding `client_identity`. |
| `trust_roots_file` | string | unset | A PEM bundle of trust roots beside the platform's. |
| `min_version` | `"1.2"` or `"1.3"` | `"1.3"` | The oldest TLS version the client speaks: `"1.3"` unless lowered to `"1.2"`, as for the listener. |

## `[terminology.endpoint.credentials.onward]`

The onward target the lane reaches on a caller's behalf, authenticating with `oauth`.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string | `""` | The identifier of the issuer of the onward tokens, whose metadata names its token endpoint unless `token_endpoint` is set. |
| `kind` | `"persons"` or `"patients"` or `"machines"` or `"federation"` | unset | Whose tokens the issuer signs: `persons` (a delegated exchange), `patients` (a patient's own token) or `federation`; required, with no default. |
| `profile` | `"rfc9068"` or `"entra"` or `"keycloak"` or `"okta"` or `"nl"` | `"rfc9068"` | The preset the issuer's profile starts from. |
| `token_endpoint` | string | `""` | The token endpoint itself; empty to discover it from `issuer`. It renders with its userinfo and its query masked. |
| `client_id` | string | `""` | The client id at this issuer; empty for the lane's own. |
| `audiences` | array of string | `[]` | The audiences an onward token may name, at least one. |
| `indicators` | array of string | `[]` | The `resource` or `audience` values the request names, as the profile's `onward_indicator` says. |
| `scope` | string | `""` | The `scope` the request names; empty for none. |
| `correlation_claim` | string | `""` | The claim a chained federation route carries from the subject token to the onward token; empty for none. |
| `cache` | boolean | `true` | Whether the lane holds the tokens it obtains until they near their `exp`. `false` exchanges a token at the issuer on every call, a setting for a performance measurement's self-test, never for production. `true` by default. |
| `actor_assertion` | boolean | `false` | Whether every token exchange sent without an actor token names the lane's client as its actor with an assertion signed by the current key of its `oauth` table's key ring (RFC 8693 §2.1; `Onward::with_actor_assertion`). `false` by default. |

## `[terminology.endpoint.credentials.onward.federation]`

What a `federation` issuer asserts, over its preset's defaults; `exchanges_from` and
`person_mapping` are required.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string | `""` | The `[auth.issuer]` this table describes, of kind `federation`. |
| `contact_point` | boolean | unset | Whether the issuer is a MyHealth@EU contact point; required, with no default. |
| `mapping` | `"iua"` or `"ehdsi"` | unset | The default sources the table starts from. |
| `fields` | table of array of table | `{}` | The sources of each field, over the mapping's. |
| `countries` | array of string | `[]` | The country codes a professional may carry. |
| `issuing_authorities` | array of string | `[]` | The issuing authorities a professional or provider may name. |
| `provider_identifier_prefixes` | array of string | `[]` | The prefixes a healthcare provider identifier must start with. |
| `attests_authorization_details` | boolean | `false` | Whether the issuer attests the `authorization_details` it puts in a token, which RFC 9396 §12 has "sent through the user agent". |
| `authorization_details_type` | string | unset | The `authorization_details` type the attributes are read from. |
| `organisation_types` | array of string | `[]` | The `authorization_details` types that state an organisation's access. |
| `presentations_claim` | string | unset | The claim holding the Verifiable Presentations of a Nuts RFC021 §6 introspection response, `vps`. |
| `user_credential_types` | array of string | `[]` | The credential types the deployment declares user-authenticated. |
| `required_fields` | array of `"professional.family_name"` or `"professional.given_name"` or `"professional.name"` or `"professional.country_code"` or `"professional.hp_identifier"` or `"professional.issuing_authority_name"` or `"professional.hp_professional_role"` or `"professional.healthcare_provider_identifier"` or `"provider.healthcare_provider_identifier"` or `"provider.issuing_authority_name"` or `"provider.healthcare_provider_name"` or `"provider.healthcare_provider_address"` or `"purpose_of_use"` or `"assurance"` or `"nl.professional_number"` or `"nl.role"` or `"nl.ura"` or `"nl.organisation_type"` or `"professional.on_behalf_of"` or `"professional.authentication_method"` or `"professional.speciality"` or `"professional.npi"` or `"professional.permissions"` or `"provider.facility_type"` or `"provider.home_community_id"` or `"point_of_care"` or `"assertion.issuer"` or `"assertion.id"` or `"assertion.not_before"` or `"assertion.not_on_or_after"` or `"trc.id"` or `"trc.not_before"` or `"trc.not_on_or_after"` or `"patient.id"` or `"patient.id_source"` or `"patient.pid_issuer_country"` or `"consent.reference"` or `"correlation_id"` or `"assertion.name_id_format"` or `"message_id"` | `[]` | The fields every token of the issuer must carry, each with a source. |
| `requires_sender_constraint` | boolean | `false` | Whether the issuer's tokens must be sender-constrained, so the issuer fails to load without `sender_constraint = "required"`. |
| `exchanges_from` | array of string | `[]` | The subject-token issuers whose persons this issuer is trusted to map to its own, when it issues onward tokens (`client::onward`). |
| `person_mapping` | string | unset | The subject-token claim, a dotted path, whose value an onward token of this issuer must carry as `professional.hp_identifier`. |

## `[terminology.endpoint.credentials.onward.assurance]`

The assurance level the issuer's tokens carry.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claim` | string | `"acr"` | The claim carrying the authentication context class, a dotted path; `acr` by default (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §2). |
| `levels` | table of `"low"` or `"substantial"` or `"high"` | `{}` | The level each claim value the issuer emits stands for; a value the map does not name carries none. |
| `minimum` | `"low"` or `"substantial"` or `"high"` | unset | The level a request held to the section must carry; none refuses nothing. |

## `[pixm]`

The IHE PIXm patient identity source the subject index asks (ITI-83) under `record.subject_index =
"pixm"`.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assigning_authority` | string | `""` | The assigning authority of the clinical domain, an absolute URI such as `urn:oid:2.999.1`: the `targetSystem` of every ITI-83 query and the `EHR_STATUS.subject.external_ref.namespace` the answered identifier is stored under. It must be one of `privacy.subject_namespaces`. |
| `method` | `"post"` or `"get"` | `"post"` | How the PIX Manager is asked: `post` (the default) or `get`. |

## `[pixm.endpoint]`

`[pixm.endpoint]`, the family's outbound endpoint: the FHIR base URL of the PIX Manager (`url`, the
`[base]` of `[base]/Patient/$ihe-pix`, PIXm §2:3.83.4.1.2), the timeout of one ITI-83 exchange, its
`retry`, the TLS (trust roots for a PIX Manager behind a private PKI, a client identity for mutual
TLS) and the credential, such as the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant whose access token every
request carries (IUA ITI-72 §3.72.4.2). Any `userinfo` in the URL is masked in every rendering.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | `""` | The service's URL (RFC 3986); required. It renders with its userinfo and its query masked, in `Debug` and when serialized. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long one whole call may take; never zero. |
| `connect_timeout` | string | unset | How long opening the connection may take; unset, only `timeout` bounds it. |

## `[pixm.endpoint.retry]`

How a failed call is tried again.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_attempts` | integer | `3` | How many times one call is tried in all; 1 tries once. |
| `initial_backoff` | duration | `"200ms"` | The wait before the second try. |
| `max_backoff` | duration | `"5s"` | The longest wait between two tries. |

## `[pixm.endpoint.tls]`

The TLS of the connection, built by the product's reader of TLS material.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client_identity` | string | unset | The client certificate chain and its private key, in one PEM. |
| `client_identity_file` | string | unset | A file holding `client_identity`. |
| `trust_roots_file` | string | unset | A PEM bundle of trust roots beside the platform's. |
| `min_version` | `"1.2"` or `"1.3"` | `"1.3"` | The oldest TLS version the client speaks: `"1.3"` unless lowered to `"1.2"`, as for the listener. |

## `[pixm.endpoint.credentials]`

The credential the calls carry: HTTP Basic or the client credentials grant.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | string | `""` | The Basic user-id. |
| `password` | string | unset | The Basic password, rendered redacted. |
| `password_file` | string | unset | The file holding the Basic password. |

## `[pixm.endpoint.credentials.oauth]`

The client credentials grant.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string | `""` | The issuer whose metadata names the token endpoint; exclusive with `token_endpoint`. |
| `token_endpoint` | string | `""` | The token endpoint itself; exclusive with `issuer`. It renders with its userinfo and its query masked. |
| `client_id` | string | `""` | The client identifier. |
| `client_auth` | `"client_secret_basic"` or `"client_secret_post"` or `"private_key_jwt"` or `"tls_client_auth"` or `"self_signed_tls_client_auth"` | `"client_secret_basic"` | How the client authenticates. |
| `client_secret` | string | unset | The client secret, rendered redacted. |
| `client_secret_file` | string | unset | The file holding the client secret. |
| `private_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file holding the private key of the client assertion under `private_key_jwt`, and of the actor assertion of an onward exchange (`credentials.onward.actor_assertion`) whatever the client authentication. |
| `kid` | string | `""` | The `kid` the assertion names; the RFC 7638 thumbprint when empty. |
| `assertion_alg` | string | unset | The algorithm the assertion is signed with; when unset, by key type, an EC key by its curve (P-256 ES256, P-384 ES384). |
| `scope` | string | `""` | The `scope` request parameter; empty for none. |
| `resource` | string | `""` | The RFC 8707 resource indicator; empty for none. |
| `audience` | string | `""` | The `audience` request parameter; empty for none. |
| `refresh_margin` | duration | `"30s"` | How long before the token expires a new one is fetched. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long one call to the authorization server may take. |
| `assertion_audience` | `"token_endpoint"` or `"issuer"` | `"token_endpoint"` | The `aud` of a `private_key_jwt` assertion: `token_endpoint` (the default) or `issuer`, which needs `issuer` set. |
| `dpop_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file of the `DPoP` key the tokens are bound to (RFC 9449). |
| `certificate_bound` | boolean | `false` | Whether the tokens are bound to the client certificate (RFC 8705 §3). |
| `security_profile` | `"oauth2"` or `"fapi2"` | `"oauth2"` | The security profile: `oauth2` (the default) or `fapi2`. |
| `mtls_alias_hosts` | array of string | `[]` | The hosts a FAPI 2.0 mutual-TLS alias may be on (RFC 8705 §5). |
| `previous_private_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file of the previous assertion key, published, never signing. |
| `previous_key_overlap` | duration | `"0s"` | How long the previous key stays published; `0s` for as long as it is set. |
| `next_private_key_file` | string | unset | The PEM file of the next assertion key, published and never signing. |
| `authorization_details` | string | `""` | The RFC 9396 `authorization_details` JSON text; empty for none. |

## `[pixm.endpoint.credentials.oauth.tls]`

The TLS of the token endpoint connection: trust roots beside the platform's, the client identity
presented over mutual TLS (RFC 8705 §2) and the minimum version. The crate reads none of it: a table
that names material resolves through the product's `TlsBuilder`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client_identity` | string | unset | The client certificate chain and its private key, in one PEM. |
| `client_identity_file` | string | unset | A file holding `client_identity`. |
| `trust_roots_file` | string | unset | A PEM bundle of trust roots beside the platform's. |
| `min_version` | `"1.2"` or `"1.3"` | `"1.3"` | The oldest TLS version the client speaks: `"1.3"` unless lowered to `"1.2"`, as for the listener. |

## `[pixm.endpoint.credentials.onward]`

The onward target the lane reaches on a caller's behalf, authenticating with `oauth`.

The table is optional.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string | `""` | The identifier of the issuer of the onward tokens, whose metadata names its token endpoint unless `token_endpoint` is set. |
| `kind` | `"persons"` or `"patients"` or `"machines"` or `"federation"` | unset | Whose tokens the issuer signs: `persons` (a delegated exchange), `patients` (a patient's own token) or `federation`; required, with no default. |
| `profile` | `"rfc9068"` or `"entra"` or `"keycloak"` or `"okta"` or `"nl"` | `"rfc9068"` | The preset the issuer's profile starts from. |
| `token_endpoint` | string | `""` | The token endpoint itself; empty to discover it from `issuer`. It renders with its userinfo and its query masked. |
| `client_id` | string | `""` | The client id at this issuer; empty for the lane's own. |
| `audiences` | array of string | `[]` | The audiences an onward token may name, at least one. |
| `indicators` | array of string | `[]` | The `resource` or `audience` values the request names, as the profile's `onward_indicator` says. |
| `scope` | string | `""` | The `scope` the request names; empty for none. |
| `correlation_claim` | string | `""` | The claim a chained federation route carries from the subject token to the onward token; empty for none. |
| `cache` | boolean | `true` | Whether the lane holds the tokens it obtains until they near their `exp`. `false` exchanges a token at the issuer on every call, a setting for a performance measurement's self-test, never for production. `true` by default. |
| `actor_assertion` | boolean | `false` | Whether every token exchange sent without an actor token names the lane's client as its actor with an assertion signed by the current key of its `oauth` table's key ring (RFC 8693 §2.1; `Onward::with_actor_assertion`). `false` by default. |

## `[pixm.endpoint.credentials.onward.keys]`

The profile keys set over the preset; `max_onward_lifetime` is required, here or in the preset.

|---|---|---|---|
| `person_key` | string | unset | `Profile::person_key`. |
| `tenant_claim` | string | unset | `Profile::tenant_claim`. |
| `client_claims` | array of string | unset | `Profile::client_claims`. |
| `impersonation_marker` | string | unset | `Profile::impersonation_marker`. |
| `expect` | table of string | unset | `Profile::expect`. |
| `user_claims` | array of string | unset | `Profile::user_claims`. |

| `max_actor_chain` | integer | unset | `Profile::max_actor_chain`. |
| `act_represents_patient` | boolean | unset | `Profile::act_represents_patient`. |
| `token_types` | array of string | unset | `Profile::token_types`. |
| `required_claims` | array of string | unset | `Profile::required_claims`. |
| `adapter` | string | unset | `Profile::adapter`. |
| `max_onward_lifetime` | string | unset | `Profile::max_onward_lifetime`, a duration such as `"10min"`. |
| `onward_grant` | `"token_exchange"` or `"jwt_bearer"` | unset | `Profile::onward_grant`. |
| `onward_indicator` | `"resource"` or `"audience"` | unset | `Profile::onward_indicator`. |
| `onward_parameters` | table of string | unset | `Profile::onward_parameters`. |
| `onward_client_id` | boolean | unset | `Profile::onward_client_id`. |

| `onward_preview` | array of `"actor_token"` | unset | `Profile::onward_preview`. |

`Profile::scope_claim`.
